title: Near-Horizon Scalar-Wave Sampling: Rindler Bounds and Schwarzschild Comparison
summary: We study classical reconstruction of an outgoing scalar-wave component from radial-shell observations. Starting from the noncompact-time Rindler metric, we construct Klein--Gordon evolution by closed quadratic forms and reduce the massless characteristic dynamics to translation in optical distance. For an initial optical interval of length $L$, a shell of width $d$, and recording time $T$, the optimal squared observability bounds are $A(T,L)=\min\{d,(T-L)_+\}$ and $B(T,L)=\min\{d,T\}$.
